transcript.answer:
Short answer
- Root cause: ledger-api processes on rcabench-worker2 hit the process file-descriptor limit (EMFILE / errno 24). The app failed to accept new connections ("accept failed: [Errno 24] Too many open files"), the readiness probe started failing (503 / connection refused) and those pods remained NotReady. Three replicas on rcabench-worker2 were affected; three replicas on rcabench-worker remained Ready.

What I found (evidence)
1. Pod distribution / readiness (current cluster state)
   - ledger-api-866db84748-2zjp4 — Ready=false — Node=rcabench-worker2
   - ledger-api-866db84748-cz4wp — Ready=false — Node=rcabench-worker2
   - ledger-api-866db84748-vv6jk — Ready=false — Node=rcabench-worker2
   - ledger-api-866db84748-md6xh — Ready=true  — Node=rcabench-worker
   - ledger-api-866db84748-r5mbh — Ready=true  — Node=rcabench-worker
   - ledger-api-866db84748-xzjxb — Ready=true  — Node=rcabench-worker

2. Pod readiness probe failures (pod descriptions)
   - The NotReady pods show readiness probe failures such as:
     - "Readiness probe failed: Get "http://10.244.1.15:8080/healthz": dial tcp 10.244.1.15:8080: connect: connection refused"
     - Later repeated: "Readiness probe failed: HTTP probe failed with statuscode: 503"
   - Readiness probe in the pod spec: http-get http://:8080/healthz timeout=1s period=5s failure=2.

3. Application logs (last hour)
   - Repeated error lines starting 2026-10-07T09:45:33Z:
     - "2026-10-07T09:45:33Z ERROR ledger-api accept failed: [Errno 24] Too many open files"
     - The same error repeated roughly every 10s for the affected pods for many minutes (dozens of occurrences up through ~09:58:03Z in the log excerpt).
   - Healthy pods on rcabench-worker show normal activity (periodic "posted batch entries=200" messages) and no EMFILE errors in the same interval.

4. Deployment / rollout context
   - Deployment has APP_VERSION=1.4.2 in the pod environment and the rollout created 6 replicas (new RS 866db84748).
   - After the rollout to 1.4.2, three pods on one node failed readiness.

5. Node health
   - rcabench-worker2 is Ready from the node status and shows no Memory/Disk/PID pressure. However, all affected pods are colocated on this node.

Why that points to file-descriptor exhaustion as the root cause
- The application error "[Errno 24] Too many open files" is the kernel/OS error when a process exceeds its allowed number of open file descriptors. The app then cannot accept new TCP connections, causing the readiness probe to fail (connection refused or HTTP 503), which makes the pod NotReady.
- The error is concentrated on the three pods that live on rcabench-worker2; replicas on rcabench-worker do not show the error. That implies a node-local limit or node-local condition (per-process limit on that node or other processes consuming descriptors), not a global cluster-wide config only.

Likely immediate explanation (most probable)
- After the 1.4.2 rollout the ledger-api process on rcabench-worker2 either:
  1) started leaking file descriptors (new bug/regression in 1.4.2), or
  2) encountered higher connection load on that node and hit the process RLIMIT_NOFILE, or
  3) the node has a lower host/process FD limit or other local processes consumed many FDs on that node.
- Any of these produces the same symptom: accept() fails with EMFILE and the pod readiness fails.

Immediate mitigations you can run now (safe, runnable commands)
- Restart the affected pods (fast, usually lowest-risk):
  - kubectl get pods -n ledger --field-selector spec.nodeName=rcabench-worker2 -o name \
    | xargs -r -n1 kubectl delete -n ledger
  This will let the scheduler place new replicas (which may land on other nodes) and recover service availability quickly.

- If you prefer to evacuate the node (safe if cluster capacity exists), cordon + drain the node:
  - kubectl cordon rcabench-worker2
  - kubectl drain rcabench-worker2 --ignore-daemonsets --delete-emptydir-data
  After pods move off, investigate the node; then uncordon:
  - kubectl uncordon rcabench-worker2

- If you need a single-pod restart:
  - kubectl delete pod ledger-api-866db84748-2zjp4 -n ledger

Diagnostics to run next (on the node / process) — exact commands to confirm the cause
(You will need SSH or access to the node to run these.)

1) Check per-process open FDs for the ledger process on rcabench-worker2:
   - pid=$(pgrep -f ledger_api)     # find the app PID (or find inside container)
   - sudo ls -l /proc/$pid/fd | wc -l
   - sudo cat /proc/$pid/limits | grep -i "open files"

2) If the app runs inside the container, exec into the container and check:
   - kubectl exec -n ledger -it <pod-name> -- sh -c 'ls -1 /proc/1/fd | wc -l; cat /proc/1/limits | grep "Max open files"'
     (replace <pod-name> with one of the affected or healthy pods appropriately)

3) List network sockets / connections (to see many TIME_WAIT or established sockets):
   - sudo ss -s
   - sudo ss -tanp | grep <pid>

4) Check host-level limits:
   - ulimit -n   # shows shell limit; check systemd unit or container runtime settings for the process

5) Inspect dmesg / syslog for kernel messages:
   - sudo dmesg | grep -i "too many open files"

Recommended longer-term fixes
- If it's an application FD leak in 1.4.2: fix the leak in the application and release a patch. Instrument the app with fd-count metrics and add unit tests / e2e tests for resource cleanup.
- Increase the process RLIMIT_NOFILE for the ledger-api process if legitimately needed:
  - Configure the container / image entrypoint to set ulimit -n to a higher value (e.g., 65536) before starting Python; or set the limit in the node/container runtime (systemd or containerd) if allowed.
  - Note: Kubernetes does not provide a direct pod spec field for RLIMIT_NOFILE; you must set it in the container process or host configuration, or via an init process in the container.
- Add FD consumption monitoring and alerting (per-pod metric: number of open fds).
- Harden readiness probes: increase timeout or reduce probe aggressiveness to avoid transient NotReady flips during short spikes (but this is a mitigation, not a fix).
- Consider pod anti-affinity to avoid placing multiple replicas on the same node, or tune the rolling update strategy so failures on one node don't reduce availability by half.

Follow-up I can do for you
- If you want, I can:
  - Restart the affected pods for you (I can show the exact kubectl commands).
  - Run the node/process diagnostics — if you can provide SSH access or run the suggested commands on rcabench-worker2 and paste output, I will interpret them and give the exact remediation steps (e.g., how to raise RLIMIT or find the leak).
  - Search code in the 1.4.2 changeset for socket-related changes that could leak FDs (if you give access to the repo).

Short checklist summary (what I completed)
- Confirmed 3/6 replicas NotReady and all on node rcabench-worker2.
- Confirmed readiness probe failures (connection refused → 503).
- Pulled logs from NotReady pods covering the past hour and found repeated "[Errno 24] Too many open files" errors beginning ~2026-10-07T09:45:33Z.
- Verified healthy replicas (on rcabench-worker) do not show the error.
- Checked node status (rcabench-worker2 is Ready; no memory/disk/PID pressure reported).

If you want immediate availability restored now, say "restart pods" or "drain node rcabench-worker2" and I will provide the exact kubectl commands (or run them if you want the command text). If you want me to help triage the node-level FD counts, run the diagnostic commands I listed and paste results.
